title: Quantized Model Market Pulse Mapper & Procurement Hypothesis Workbook
creator: Mariana Ortiz
description: Goal: produce a concise, operational deliverable that helps Product + Sales + SRE teams reason about when to accept quantized model variants (2/4/8-bit), the procurement triggers for switching providers, and signal thresholds that should surface in the Console and SRE runbooks. This ticket scopes research, experiments, and a buyer-facing hypothesis workbook that maps quality vs. latency vs. unit-cost tradeoffs and recommended mitigation playbooks.
background: Recent vendor movement towards aggressive quantized releases and model packaging (e.g., new 4-bit variants with mixed-precision kernels) has created buyer uncertainty. Sales asks for concrete guidance: which quantized variants are acceptable for which enterprise use-cases, what regressions to expect, and how to operationalize fallbacks without breaking SLAs. We need an evidence-backed rubric and a small set of telemetry-driven signals to power Console alerts and procurement handbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Market Pulse dashboard prototype with weekly availability and quantization-variant coverage by region
Procurement Hypothesis Workbook: decision matrix mapping use-cases to acceptable quantization bands and fallback rules
Synthetic workload and field-interview results (n=8 enterprise customers) demonstrating quality delta ranges across quantization settings
A short runbook for SRE/Customer Success describing automated rollback triggers and compensation controls
Executive one-pager summarizing key procurement triggers and recommended SLA language
tasks: Define 6 canonical enterprise workload profiles (RAG-embedding-heavy, chat-UI, short-query search, summarization, multi-turn chaining, code-editing)
Design synthetic workloads for each profile (input distributions, token-length buckets, correctness metrics)
Select 3 vendor model families to test (open-source and partner-hosted) and identify quantized variants to compare
Run controlled A/B experiments measuring latency, per-token cost, and quality (ROUGE/ExactMatch/embedding-cosine) across quantization levels
Recruit and run 8 targeted customer interviews exploring tolerance thresholds and procurement constraints
Construct procurement hypothesis workbook and decision rubric with clear thresholds (latency %, quality delta, cost delta)
Prototype Market Pulse dashboard (Grafana/Console view) ingesting our synthetic/field telemetry
Write SRE runbook snippets and Console alert definitions for 'quantization-caused-quality-drop' and 'vendor-variant-unavailable'
Workshop findings with Sales and Legal to draft procurement clauses (fallback SLAs, roll-forward allowances)

risk_and_open_questions:
- Risk: synthetic workloads may understate real-world prompt engineering failure modes.
- Q: which metric best captures 'perceived quality' for summarization vs. code? (ROUGE vs. behavior tests)
- Risk: vendors may change quantization packaging mid-experiment, invalidating runs. Plan to snapshot model binaries and hashes.
notes: Use field interview transcripts to calibrate acceptance thresholds. Prioritize building a minimal telemetry hook in the Console to flag 'quality regression after quantization' so customer success can surface early. Coordinate with Eng to ensure one offline inference binary snapshot per variant. Expect follow-up ticket to instrument automated canaries for production traffic.
